rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses the believer to honor him, as He addressed Moses.
rows.anchor: للمؤمن { ياأيتها النفس } إكراماً له كما كلم موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the address is delivered by an angel.
rows.anchor: أو يكون على لسان ملك { المطمئنة } الآمنة التي لا يستفزها خوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense is the believing soul, secure from fear and grief.
rows.anchor: { المطمئنة } الآمنة التي لا يستفزها خوف ولا حزن وهي النفس المؤمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is settled in truth by certainty, with no doubt troubling it.
rows.anchor: أو المطمئنة إلى الحق التي سكّنها ثلج اليقين فلا يخالجها شك

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Abū's reading adds “secure” before “tranquil,” supporting the first interpretation.
rows.anchor: ويشهد للتفسير الأول قراءة أبي { يأَيَّتُهَا النفس الآمنةالمطمئنة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be made at death, resurrection, or entry into Paradise.
rows.anchor: وإنما يقال لها عند الموت أو عند البعث أو عند دخول الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Return to your Lord” can mean return to the appointed meeting with Him.
rows.anchor: { ارجعى إلى } موعد { رَبِّكِ } أو ثواب ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, return to your Lord means return to His reward.
rows.anchor: { ارجعى إلى } موعد { رَبِّكِ } أو ثواب ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is pleased with God for what it has been given.
rows.anchor: { رَاضِيَةٍ } من الله بما أوتيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is pleasing to God because of what it did.
rows.anchor: { مَّرْضِيَّةً } عند الله بما عملت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enter among God's righteous servants and join their company.
rows.anchor: { فادخلى فِى عِبَادِى } في جملة عبادي الصالحين فانتظمي في سلكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul enters God's Garden together with the righteous servants.
rows.anchor: { وادخلى جَنَّتِى } معهم . وقال أبو عبيدة : أي مع عبادي

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda takes “among My servants” to mean with or among God's chosen servants.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : أي مع عبادي أو بين عبادي أي خواصي كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the soul to mean the spirit, entering the bodies of God's servants.
rows.anchor: وقيل : النفس الروح ومعناه فادخلي في أجساد عبادي كقراءة عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading has “in the body of My servant.”
rows.anchor: كقراءة عبد الله بن مسعود { فِي جسد عبدي } ولما مات ابن عباس بالطائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Ibn ʿAbbās died at Ṭāʾif, an unfamiliar bird entered his bier; this verse was recited at his grave by an unknown person.
rows.anchor: ولما مات ابن عباس بالطائف جاء طائر لم ير على خلقته فدخل في نعشه فلما دفن تليت هذه الآية على شفير القبر ولم يدر من تلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion of revelation is Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
rows.anchor: قيل : نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported occasion is Khubayb ibn ʿAdī: after being crucified facing away from Medina, he prayed for his face to turn toward the qibla; God turned it, and no one could turn it back.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في خبيب بن عدي الذي صلبه أهل مكة وجعلوا وجهه إلى المدينة فقال : اللهم إن كان لي عندك خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may apply generally to believers: the wording's general scope governs rather than a particular occasion.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي عامة في المؤمنين إذ العبرة لعموم اللفظ لا لخصوص السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lubadan means abundant wealth, from lubda, a mass packed or gathered together.
rows.anchor: أي كثيراً جمع لبدة وهو ما تلبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He boasts of spending much on what pre-Islamic Arabs called generosity and noble deeds.
rows.anchor: يريد كثرة ما أنفقه فيما كان أهل الجاهلية يسمونها مكارم ومعالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He spent to show off and boast; God saw him and kept watch over him.
rows.anchor: حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رياء وافتخاراً يعني أن الله تعالى كان يراه وكان عليه رقيباً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds the human of His favors, including two eyes with which to see visible things.
rows.anchor: { أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ عَيْنَيْنِ } يبصر بهما المرئيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaghwā means their transgression; their excess was what drove them to deny the truth.
rows.anchor: بطغيانها إذ الحامل لهم على التكذيب طغيانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's messenger here is Ṣāliḥ, peace be upon him.
rows.anchor: { فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ الله } صالح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥ warns them to protect God's she-camel and its watering; “God's she-camel” is accusative for warning, like “the lion, the lion.”
rows.anchor: { نَاقَةُ الله } نصب على التحذير أي احذروا عقرها { وسقياها } كقولك : الأسد الأسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied Ṣāliḥ's warning that punishment would come if they acted as they did.
rows.anchor: { فَكَذَّبُوهُ } فيما حذرهم منه من نزول العذاب إن فعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole people are credited with hamstringing the she-camel although one man did it, because they approved his act.
rows.anchor: { فَعَقَرُوهَا } أي الناقة أسند الفعل إليهم وإن كان العاقر واحداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God annihilated them because they denied the messenger and hamstrung the she-camel.
rows.anchor: { فَدَمْدمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ } أهلكهم هلاك استئصال { بِذَنبِهِمْ } بسبب ذنبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment leveled them all; neither young nor old escaped it.
rows.anchor: { فَسَوَّاهَا } فسوى الدمدمة عليهم لم يفلت منها صغيرهم ولا كبيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Layl is Meccan and has twenty-one verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الليل احدى وعشرون آية مكية بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night may cover the sun, as in the night covering it.
rows.anchor: أما الشمس من قوله { واليل إِذَا يغشاها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may cover the day, as in the day covering the night.
rows.anchor: أو النهار من قوله { يغشى اليل النهار } [ الأعراف : 54 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Or it may be everything that darkness hides.
rows.anchor: أو كل شيء يواريه بظلامه من قوله { إِذَا وَقَبَ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human effort and deeds differ; the following verses explain the ways in which they differ.
rows.anchor: إن عملكم لمختلف وبيان الاختلاف فيما فصل على أثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generous person gives the rights due from his wealth.
rows.anchor: { فَأَمَّا مَنْ أعطى } حقوق ماله { واتقى } ربه فاجتنب محارمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fears his Lord and avoids His prohibitions.
rows.anchor: { واتقى } ربه فاجتنب محارمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā may mean the most beautiful religion, Islam.
rows.anchor: { وَصَدَّقَ بالحسنى } بالملة الحسنى وهي ملة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the finest reward, Paradise.
rows.anchor: أو بالمثوبة الحسنى وهي الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Or it is the excellent declaration “There is no god but God.”
rows.anchor: أو بالكلمة الحسنى وهي لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares such a person for the easier way: acting in what pleases his Lord.
rows.anchor: { فَسَنُيَسّرُهُ لليسرى } فسنهيئه للخلة اليسرى وهي العمل بما يرضاه ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is miserly with his wealth.
rows.anchor: { وَأَمَّا مَن بَخِلَ } بماله { واستغنى } عن ربه فلم يتقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may regard himself as independent of his Lord and so not fear Him.
rows.anchor: { واستغنى } عن ربه فلم يتقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he is absorbed in worldly desires instead of the bliss of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أو استغنى بشهوات الدنيا عن نعيم العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying al-ḥusnā means denying Islam or Paradise.
rows.anchor: { وَكَذَّبَ بالحسنى } بالإسلام أو الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares him for the difficult course leading to Hell, making obedience his hardest and most burdensome task.
rows.anchor: { فَسَنُيَسّرُهُ للعسرى } للخلة المؤدية إلى النار فتكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه وأشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation names the good path “easy” for its easy outcome, and the evil path “difficult” for its difficult outcome.
rows.anchor: أو سمى طريقة الخير باليسرى لأن عاقبتها اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the easy and difficult ways are the paths to Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: أو أراد بهما طريقي الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wealth will not help him when he perishes.
rows.anchor: { وَمَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تردى } ولم ينفعه ماله إذا هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taraddā derives from al-radā, destruction, and can mean he perished.
rows.anchor: وتردى تفعّل من الردى وهو الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means falling into the grave or into the depths of Hell.
rows.anchor: أو تردى في القبر أو في قعر جهنم أي سقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes to guide by setting out proofs and explaining the revealed laws.
rows.anchor: إن علينا الإرشاد إلى الحق بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the present and afterlife belong to God, the misguidance of the lost neither harms Him nor the guidance of the guided benefits Him.
rows.anchor: فلا يضرنا ضلال من ضل ولا ينفعنا اهتداء من اهتدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, both lives are God's; whoever seeks them from another has taken the wrong path.
rows.anchor: أو أنهما لنا فمن طلبهما من غيرنا فقد أخطأ الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the most wretched enters that Fire to remain there eternally.
rows.anchor: { لاَ يصلاها } لا يدخلها للخلود فيها { إِلاَّ الأشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched is the unbeliever who denied the messengers and turned away from faith.
rows.anchor: إلا الكافر الذي كذب الرسل وأعرض عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person kept far from the Fire is the believer, the pious one.
rows.anchor: { وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا } وسيبعد منها { الأتقى } المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives his wealth to the poor, seeking purity before God rather than showing off or seeking fame.
rows.anchor: { الذى يُؤْتِى مَالَهُ } للفقراء { يتزكى } من الزكاء أي يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكياً لا يريد به رياء ولا سمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “purifying himself” substitutes for “gives,” it has no syntactic case because it falls within the relative clause.
rows.anchor: و { يتزكى } إن جعلته بدلاً من { يؤتى } فلا محل له لأنه داخل في حكم الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If taken as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in “he gives,” it is accusative.
rows.anchor: وإن جعلته حالاً من الضمير في { يؤتى } فمحله النصب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reads “most wretched” as “wretched” (unbeliever) and “most pious” as “pious” (believer): the generic classes, not only the most extreme individuals, burn or are saved.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الأشقى بمعنى الشقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the passage compares outstanding figures among polytheists and believers, speaking as if the Fire were made only for one and Paradise only for the other.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported identification makes the most wretched Abū Jahl and the most pious Abū Bakr.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafī says these verses refute the Murjiʾite claim that only an unbeliever enters Hell.
rows.anchor: وفيه بطلان زعم المرجئة لأنهم يقولون لا يدخل النار إلا كافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā is Meccan and has eleven verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الضحى مكية وهى إحدى عشر آية بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḍuḥā is the morning's early part, when the sun has risen higher.
rows.anchor: المراد وقت الضحى وهو صدر النهار حين ترتفع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forenoon may be singled out because God spoke to Moses then and the magicians fell prostrate then.
rows.anchor: وإنما خص وقت الضحى بالقسم لأنها الساعة التي كلم الله فيها موسى عليه السلام وألقى فيها السحرة سجداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the oath is by the whole day, paired with the night that grows still.
rows.anchor: أو النهار كله لمقابلته بالليل في قوله { واليل إِذَا سجى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listing earlier favors teaches the Prophet to measure future grace from past grace, expect good and more, and not lose patience or feel constricted.
rows.anchor: ثم عدد عليه نعمه من أول حاله ليقيس المترقب من فضل الله على ما سلف منه لئلا يتوقع إلا الحسنى وزيادة الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Found” here means “knew,” and “you” and “orphan” are its two accusative objects.
rows.anchor: وهو من الوجود الذي بمعنى العلم والمنصوبان مفعولاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When his parents died, God sheltered him with his uncle Abū Ṭālib, who took him in, fostered him, and raised him.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ألم تكن يتيماً حين مات أبواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Astray” means not yet knowing the signs of prophethood, the laws of the revealed way, or the path of revelation; God then taught him the laws and Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: أي غير عالم ولا واقف على معالم النبوة وأحكام الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says he lost the road to Syria while traveling with Abū Ṭālib, who returned him to the caravan.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ضل في طريق الشام حين خرج به أبو طالب فرده إلى القافلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This cannot mean deviation from truth: from the beginning until revelation he was protected from idol worship and the filthy conduct of sinners.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يفهم به عدول عن حق ووقوع في غي فقد كان عليه الصلاة السلام من أول حاله إلى نزول الوحي عليه معصوماً من عبادة الأوثان وقاذورات أهل الفسق والعصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀʾilan means poor; God made him wealthy.
rows.anchor: { وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلاً } فقيراً { فأغنى } فأغناك بمال خديجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was enriched either through Khadīja's wealth or through spoils granted to him.
rows.anchor: فأغناك بمال خديجة أو بمال أفاء عليك من الغنائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the answer to the oath, and “human” denotes the species as a whole.
rows.anchor: وجواب القسم { لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان } وهو جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the human in the finest proportion: the best form, appearance, and arrangement of limbs.
rows.anchor: { فِى أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ } في أحسن تعديل لشكله وصورته وتسوية أعضائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-ʿAlaq is Meccan and consists of nineteen verses.
rows.anchor: سورة العلق مكية ، وهى تسع عشرة آية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid report that this was the first sūra revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد : هى أول سورة نزلت

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that al-Fātiḥa was the first revelation, followed by Sūrat al-Qalam.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن الفاتحة أول ما نزل ثم سورة القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the name of your Lord” is in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase: begin with the Lord's name when reading.
rows.anchor: النصب على الحال . أي : اقرأ مفتتحاً باسم ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense is, say “In God's name,” then read “the One who created.”
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل : قل باسم الله ثم اقرأ الذي خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “created” is omitted because God alone is the source and creator.
rows.anchor: لأن المعنى الذي حصل منه الخلق واستأثر به لا خالق سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, supply “created everything”: the unqualified wording gives no basis to prefer one created thing as the omitted object.
rows.anchor: أو تقديره خلق كل شيء فيتناول كل مخلوق لأنه مطلق فليس بعض المخلوقات بتقديره أولى من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is singled out from all creation for its nobility and because revelation is addressed to it.
rows.anchor: تخصيص للإنسان بالذكر من بين ما يتناوله الخلق لشرفه ولأن التنزيل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wording first leaves the created thing unspecified and then identifies it as the human, magnifying the creation and its wondrous nature.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد الذي خلق الإنسان إلا أنه ذكر مبهماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “clots” is used instead of singular ʿalaqa because “human” has a collective sense.
rows.anchor: { مِنْ عَلَقٍ } وإنما جمع ولم يقل من علقة لأن الإنسان في معنى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Akram describes the Lord's complete generosity, surpassing every other generous giver.
rows.anchor: { اقرأ وَرَبُّكَ الأكرم } الذي له الكمال في زيادة كرمه على كل كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He bestows favors on His servants and bears with their unbelief and ingratitude, delaying punishment; teaching knowledge is the supreme generosity of imparting benefits.
rows.anchor: باده النعم ويحلم عنهم ، فلا يعاجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught writing by means of the pen.
rows.anchor: { الذى عَلَّمَ } الكتابة { بالقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's complete generosity appears in teaching people what they did not know and moving them from the darkness of ignorance to the light of knowledge.
rows.anchor: فدل على كمال كرمه بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing has immense benefits: it records sciences and wisdom, preserves earlier reports and revealed books, and is indispensable to religious and worldly affairs; the pen and script alone show God's subtle wisdom.
rows.anchor: ونبه على فضل علم الكتابة لما فيه من المنافع العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the one who responds to God's favor with unbelief and transgression; the prior context makes that person implicit.
rows.anchor: { كَلاَّ } ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse, through the end of the sūra, was revealed concerning Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل إلى آخر السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that a person sees himself as self-sufficient; with verbs of thought, “I saw myself” means “I knew myself.”
rows.anchor: { أن رءاه } أن رأى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Self-sufficient” is the second object of “saw”; if raʾā meant physical sight, the two pronouns could not both be its objects.
rows.anchor: ولو كانت بمعنى الإبصار لامتنع في فعلها الجمع بين الضميرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift of address makes this a threat to the transgressor about the outcome of his excess.
rows.anchor: تهديد للإنسان من عاقبة الطغيان على طريق الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rajʿā is a verbal noun meaning return: the person returns to his Lord, who will requite his transgression.
rows.anchor: والرجعى مصدر بمعنى الرجوع ، أي إن رجوعك

none: The segment contains only the verse text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person forbidding the worshipper is Abū Jahl, and the servant he forbids is Muḥammad praying.
rows.anchor: أي : أرأيت أبا جهل ينهى محمداً عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the forbidding person is on a sound path in what he forbids: worship of God.
rows.anchor: أي إن كان ذلك الناهي على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه من عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It asks whether he commands virtue and piety in what he himself considers worship of idols.
rows.anchor: أو كان آمراً بالمعروف والتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative is that the forbidding person denies the truth and turns away from it, as Nasafī says he does.
rows.anchor: أرأيت إن كان ذلك الناهي مكذباً بالحق متولياً عنه كما نقول نحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God observes the person's guidance or error and requites him according to his state; this is a threat.
rows.anchor: ويطلع على أحواله من هداه وضلاله فيجازيه على حسب حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The one who forbids” and the conditional clause are the two objects of the first “Have you seen?”; its omitted answer is supplied from the second condition, while the repeated question adds emphasis.
rows.anchor: { الذى ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية مفعولا { أَرَأَيْتَ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes Abū Jahl for forbidding worship of God and commanding worship of idols.
rows.anchor: { كَلاَّ } ردع لأبي جهل عن نهيه عن عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he does not desist, God will seize him by the forelock and drag him by it into the Fire.
rows.anchor: { لَّئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ } عما هو فيه { لَنَسْفَعاً بالناصية } لنأخذن بناصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safʿ is to seize something and pull it forcefully.
rows.anchor: والسفع : القبض على الشيء وجذبه بشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is written with alif in the muṣḥaf according to pause spelling; the definite article replaces possession because the referent's forelock is known.
rows.anchor: في المصحف بالألف على حكم الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A lying, sinful forelock” is an apposition to the forelock mentioned before.
rows.anchor: { نَاصِيَةٍ } بدل من { الناصية } لأنها وصفت بالكذب والخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjectives transfer lying and sin figuratively from the owner to his forelock; this is more elegant and forceful than calling him a liar and sinner directly.
rows.anchor: عن الإسناد المجازي وهما لصاحبها حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nādī is the meeting place where a group gathers; here it means the people who gather there.
rows.anchor: النادي المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abū Jahl found the Prophet praying, challenged him for ignoring his prohibition, and boasted that he had the largest gathering in the valley; the passage was revealed then.
rows.anchor: روي أن أبا جهل مر بالنبي عليه السلام وهو يصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabāniya is the language's term for a guard or enforcer, singular zabniyya, from pushing; it refers here to the angels of punishment.
rows.anchor: والزبانية لغة الشرط الواحد زبنية من الزبن وهو الدفع

rows.speaker: عنه عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet said that if Abū Jahl called his gathering, the angels of punishment would seize him in plain sight.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام " لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية عياناً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nādī is the meeting place where a group gathers; here it means the people who gather there.
rows.anchor: النادي المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abū Jahl found the Prophet praying, challenged him for ignoring his prohibition, and boasted that he had the largest gathering in the valley; the passage was revealed then.
rows.anchor: روي أن أبا جهل مر بالنبي عليه السلام وهو يصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabāniya is the language's term for a guard or enforcer, singular zabniyya, from pushing; it refers here to the angels of punishment.
rows.anchor: والزبانية لغة الشرط الواحد زبنية من الزبن وهو الدفع

rows.speaker: عنه عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet said that if Abū Jahl called his gathering, the angels of punishment would seize him in plain sight.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام " لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية عياناً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not obey Abū Jahl: remain steadfast in disobeying him, as in the command not to obey the deniers.
rows.anchor: { لاَ تُطِعْهُ } أي اثبت على ما أنت عليه من عصيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Prostrate” means persist in prostration, that is, continue praying.
rows.anchor: { واسجد } ودم على سجودك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Draw near to your Lord by prostration.
rows.anchor: { واقترب } وتقرب إلى ربك بالسجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that the servant is nearest to his Lord when prostrating.
rows.anchor: فإن أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه إذا سجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanūd means intensely ungrateful, particularly for his Lord's blessings.
rows.anchor: وجواب القسم { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } لكفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may be fiercely attached to wealth, meaning miserly and withholding.
rows.anchor: وإنه لأجل حب المال لبخيل ممسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he is powerful in his love of wealth but weak in his love of worshipping God.
rows.anchor: أو إنه لحب المال لقوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-ʿAṣr is disputed as Meccan or Medinan and consists of three verses.
rows.anchor: سورة العصر مختلف فيها ، وهى ثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may be by the ʿAṣr prayer because of its merit; Ḥafṣa's codex identifies the “middle prayer” as ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: بدليل قوله تعالى : { والصلاوة الوسطى } [ البقرة : 238 ] صلاة العصر في مصحف حفصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer is especially difficult at day's end, when people are occupied with trade, earnings, and livelihoods.
rows.anchor: ولأن التكليف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجاراتهم ومكاسبهم آخر النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the oath is by afternoon, as by forenoon, because both times display signs of God's power.
rows.anchor: أو أقسم بالعشي كما أقسم بالضحى لما فيها من دلائل القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Or it is an oath by time, whose passing contains many kinds of marvels.
rows.anchor: أو أقسم بالزمان لما في مروره من أصناف العجائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's response says humanity as a species is in loss through its transactions.
rows.anchor: أي جنس الإنسان لفي خسران من تجاراتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do good are exceptions: they trade this world for the afterlife, gaining profit and felicity.
rows.anchor: فإنهم اشتروا الآخرة بالدنيا فربحوا وسعدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth is the established matter that cannot rightly be denied: all good, including God's oneness, obedience, and following His books and messengers.
rows.anchor: { وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بالحق } بالأمر الثابت الذي لا يسوغ إنكاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They urge one another to avoid sins, obey God, and endure the trials God sends His servants.
rows.anchor: { وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بالصبر } عن المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both instances of “urge one another” are past-tense verbs coordinated with the preceding past-tense verb.
rows.anchor: في الموضعين فعل ماضٍ معطوف على ماض قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Māʿūn is disputed as Meccan or Medinan and has seven verses.
rows.anchor: مختلف فيها ، وهي سبع آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether you know who denies the recompense, as if to identify him for one who does not know.
rows.anchor: أي هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء من هو إن لم تعرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier of the recompense violently shoves the orphan away, treating him harshly and abusively, and drives him off with rude rebuke.
rows.anchor: أي يدفعه دفعاً عنيفاً بجفوة وأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning continues by specifying the worshippers meant: those heedless of prayer, who show off and withhold alms or useful aid.
rows.anchor: { فَوَيْلٌ لّلْمُصَلّينَ الذين هُمْ عَن صلاتهم سَاهُونَ الذين هُمْ يُرَاءونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation identifies hypocrites: they avoid private prayer because they do not believe it obligatory, but pray publicly to show off.
rows.anchor: يعني بهذا المنافقين لا يصلونها سراً ؛ لأنهم لا يعتقدون وجوبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another description is hypocrites who outwardly count themselves among worshippers but neglect prayer, seek neither nearness nor fulfillment of duty, go through motions mindlessly, display worship, and withhold alms and useful things.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فويل للمنافقين الذين يدخلون أنفسهم في جملة المصلين صورة

rows.speaker: أنس والحسن
rows.claim: Anas and al-Ḥasan say “about their prayer” means neglecting and turning away from it, the behavior of hypocrites; “within their prayer” would mean distraction by Satan or one's thoughts, which also befalls Muslims, including the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس والحسن قالا : الحمد لله الذي قال { عَن صلاتهم } ولم يقل

rows.speaker: أنس والحسن
rows.claim: They distinguish forgetfulness “in prayer,” caused by Satanic whisper or one's thoughts, from neglecting prayer; this ordinary distraction may affect any Muslim, and the Prophet himself sometimes forgot in prayer.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «في » أن السهو يعتريهم فيها بوسوسة شيطان أو حديث نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riyāʾ is a reciprocal form from showing: the performer displays his deed to people, who respond with praise and admiration.
rows.anchor: والمراءاة مفاعلة من الإراءة ؛ لأن المرائي يرائي الناس عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Displaying obligatory worship is not showing off because it should be public; concealing voluntary worship is better, unless it is displayed to encourage imitation, which is good.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائياً بإظهار الفرائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-māʿūn means the obligatory alms, zakāt.
rows.anchor: والماعون : الزكاة . وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says al-māʿūn is the everyday lending of tools such as an axe, pot, bucket, or fire-striker.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : ما يتعاور في العادة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha says al-māʿūn is water, fire, and salt.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها : الماء والنار والملح
